theBugThisSeamHADToFixFirst.finding: MEASURED, not inferred. `tryFoldActivatedRewindBranch` returned null only for `ROOT_EVENT_BRANCH_ID` ('root'), but S1's mirror installs a mirrored stream's genesis head on MATCH_BASELINE_BRANCH_ID ('main') — `EVENT_HISTORY_GENESIS_BACKFILL_SQL` copies `head.branch_id` from `event_journal_stream_heads`, and `MatchStreamJournalMirror.toMatchJournalBatch` names 'main' when no effective head exists yet. So a HEALTHY, never-rewound, mirrored match reached the rewind fold, which asked `matchStoreBranchSegmentReader` for branch 'main'. That reader refuses every branch but 'root' by name (`unknown-branch`, matchStoreBranchSegmentReader.ts:87-95) because the match store holds exactly one line of history.
theBugThisSeamHADToFixFirst.measuredConsequence: The whole match failed to recover at boot. Captured verbatim in the RED log: `[MatchRecovery] failed to rebuild match match-recovery-journal-head EventHistoryBranchError: A match store holds only the 'root' branch; 'main' has no events` — thrown from ServerMatchHostRewindRebuild.ts:93, caught by MatchRecovery's per-match try, pushed to `failed`, no host. Inert in production (mode 'off' means no head is ever installed), reachable the moment S1's mirror is on for a stream.
theBugThisSeamHADToFixFirst.fix: The live-path test is the SET, not 'root' alone. There is no activated path on a live-path head and no tail to supersede; S4's ordinary path owns those streams.

sharedLivePathSet.change: `LIVE_PATH_BRANCH_IDS` + `isLivePathBranchId(branchId)` moved out of `ServerMatchHostBranchAdmission.ts` (where it was a module-private const, never exported, so no test imported it) to sit beside `MATCH_BASELINE_BRANCH_ID`, which it contains.
sharedLivePathSet.why: Three call sites now ask 'does this head mean a rewind happened?' — the live admission consult, the boot fold, and the recovery consult. Two definitions of that set is exactly the drift `prefer-uniformity` forbids. The admission's behaviour is unchanged: `isLivePathBranchId(head.branchId) || head.branchId === ctx.servedBranchId` is the same predicate it evaluated before.

theConsult.startedSource: `deriveMatchJournalAuthorityStartedHead` — S3a/S3b's single source of 'started', never the `mp_journal_authority_started` marker. One source, reused rather than re-derived.
theConsult.unavailableDecision: `unavailable` (port present, capability database not open) answers `legacy`. That is the SAME answer `tryFoldActivatedRewindBranch` already gives in that state (`if (!sqlite.isInitialized()) return null`), and production builds the store with no capabilityDb (`getDefaultMatchStore.ts`), so refusing here would block recovery for every ordinary match in a process that never opened the campaign file — the 11-regression shape S3b measured at the rollback-reader boundary. Recovery must not hold two opinions about whether the journal can speak. A stream with no head has no journal claim to contradict, so nothing is being silently preferred.
theConsult.divergenceRule: Both the revision AND the count are compared: `revisionForMatchSequence(lastSequence)` and `events.length` against `readEffectiveStreamHead(...).revision`. Any disagreement -> `diverged`.
theConsult.boundedRebuild: The returned events are filtered to `revisionForMatchSequence(sequence) <= head.revision`. The divergence gate makes that bound exact today; stating it is what keeps 'rebuilt from the journal head' true if the gate ever loosens.

theRefusal.reason: 'partial-history', an EXISTING member of `AuthorityRecoveryBlockedReason` — the frozen union is not extended, so no other suite's typed pin moves.
theRefusal.whyThatMember: `checkpointRecoveryPort` emits it for exactly this shape: a trusted base that was admitted, then a tail that does not continue it (AuthorityRecoveryPort.ts:265). A journal head at revision R with a match log that ends somewhere else is that sentence.
theRefusal.effect: `failed` carries the matchId, `blocked` carries `{matchId, reason:'partial-history', evidence:[...]}`, and NO host is built or registered — the match serves nothing.
theRefusal.notQuarantined: Deliberate. `quarantineAuthorityCorruption` filters on QUARANTINABLE = sequence-gap / broken-lineage / duplicate-receipt / missing-digest, and 'partial-history' is not one: a mirror that fell behind is a desynchronized copy, not authority data that is WRONG. Calling the quarantine helper here would be a no-op, so it is not called.

sharedTail.change: `registerRecoveredHost(hosts, store, matchId, state)` extracted in MatchRecovery.ts and used by BOTH the journal path and the legacy checkpoint path.
sharedTail.why: So the two paths cannot drift on the order the cursors are restored in — `restorePersistedViewerDeliveries()` BEFORE `resumePendingEventPublications()` (umbrella 7.1). One duplication of that five-line tail would have been the first step toward two different recoveries.

seedingDecision.question: Task 1.4's parent brief required a choice: seed the mirror at match creation, or restrict S4 to head-and-branch reads and record the seeding as owed by 1.7.
seedingDecision.chosen: RESTRICT TO HEAD-AND-BRANCH READS. The seeding is recorded as owed by task 1.7 (S6).
justification: design.md's own words for S4 are 'rebuilds the live host from the journal head AND THE EFFECTIVE BRANCH, not from the legacy event table alone' — head-and-branch, not journal event bytes. The already-shipped rewound path reads its bytes from the match store through `matchStoreBranchSegmentReader` too (`readActivatedBranchGameEvents`); the journal supplies which branch and how far. Doing the same on the ordinary path is ONE mechanism, not a second one.

The bytes cannot honestly come from the journal tail on this snapshot. `ServerMatchHost.create` persists opening events via `persistInitialEvents` -> `ServerMatchHostEvents` -> `store.appendEvent`, which is not the `appendCommandBatch` boundary S1's mirror hooks. Verified independently in the S2 review (`r4-s2-live-head-admission-review-20260915.json`, `4_createPathFinding`, `verified: true`) and re-measured here: prefix B's create-path row shows the follow-up batch mirroring a refusal (`getProcessShadowMismatchCount() === 1`) and NO effective head installed. A journal-tail rebuild would rebuild an incomplete session.

That same review scoped the fix: 'BLOCKING FOR S6, NOT FOR S2 ... Task 1.7 (S6, the reviewed cutover flag with shadow parity) at the LATEST — that is the box whose promise the gap falsifies. Task 1.4 (S4) is the first consumer that breaks without it and must state its dependency.' This receipt states it.

S4 is CORRECT without the seed, and that is the load-bearing half of the decision: a stream whose create events outran the mirror never gets a head at all, so it takes the legacy path, pinned byte-identical (row 2 and row 4). A stream whose head lags its log is refused typed (row 3). Neither shape can silently serve a wrong history.
seedingDecision.jcsUndefinedNote: The canonicalizer's contract is untouched, as instructed. The JCS-undefined refusal on host opening events is handled where the S3b and checkpoint-door fixtures already handle it — a JSON round-trip in the TEST fixture (`openingEvents()`), which is legitimate because the store only ever hands back parsed JSON. No production input shaping was added, because with the head-and-branch restriction no production site mirrors an opening event.
seedingDecision.whatIsOwed: Seeding the mirror at match creation (or routing `persistInitialEvents` through the batch boundary), so a created match has a journal head and shadow parity is achievable. Owner: task 1.7 (S6). Prefix B's create-path row is the executable record of the gap and will go red the day the seeding lands.

rr1.measurement: MEASURED in-session, not inferred: a better-sqlite3 handle opened exactly as `SQLiteService` opens one (`new Database(path)` at SQLiteService.ts:80, then `journal_mode = WAL` and `foreign_keys = ON`) reports `PRAGMA busy_timeout` = 5000. Log: rr1-busy-timeout-20260915.log.
rr1.consequenceForRR1: RR-1's premise as written in `r4-s1-journal-batches-review-20260915.json` ('No busy_timeout pragma ... so a mirror append contending with any other campaign writer throws SQLITE_BUSY immediately') is incorrect at the driver level: better-sqlite3 applies a 5000 ms default busy timeout with no pragma set. The RESIDUAL is therefore narrower than the review stated — a mirror still desynchronizes permanently if a lock is held longer than 5 s — but it is not an 'ordinary concurrent load' failure.
rr1.doesS4CloseIt: PARTIALLY, and only in the safe direction. S4 does NOT add mirror catch-up. What it adds is that a stream whose mirror fell behind is now DETECTED at boot and refused typed instead of silently serving the legacy log against a stale head. Catch-up (or a decision that shadow mode must not refuse) remains owed by S6 / task 1.7.

rows: 1. (a) RED->GREEN. A mirrored stream restarts through its journal head: mode 'shadow', first batch mirrored so the baseline head is installed, cold reopen, `recoverActiveMatches` -> no failures, no blocks, and `digestReplayCheckpointState(host.getSessionForTests())` equals the pre-restart digest of the same fold. The row asserts `effectiveHeadBranchId() === 'main'` before recovering, so a green cannot come from a stream that quietly had no head.
2. (b) PIN, green at base and after. No head (mode 'off', events appended one at a time): recovery is the legacy rebuild, same digest, no blocks. This is the byte-identical clause.

3. (c) RED->GREEN. Head present, legacy log diverged by one append straight past the batch boundary: `hosts` does not contain the match, `failed` is exactly `[MATCH_ID]`, and `blocked` is exactly one `partial-history` entry whose evidence names both revisions (`journal head 'main' at revision 2; match log holds 3 events through revision 3`). The host does not serve.

4. (d) PIN + the owed gap. The create path at the store boundary — opening events through `appendEvent`, then a real command batch: the mirror runs, refuses, records the shadow tripwire (`getProcessShadowMismatchCount() === 1`), and installs NO head; recovery therefore stays on the legacy path and the match recovers normally.

risksFlaggedForTheOwner.risk: The divergence refusal treats a lagging SHADOW mirror as grounds to refuse the whole match at boot. At mode 'shadow' the legacy log is still the authority, so a mirror that fell behind arguably should not stop a healthy match from serving. The parent brief was explicit ('refuse typed rather than silently preferring either'), and refusing is the fail-closed direction, so it is implemented as instructed — but S6 (task 1.7) should decide whether the refusal is gated on mode 'enabled' or whether shadow gets a repair path instead. Inert today: at mode 'off' no head is ever installed, so the arm cannot fire.

The journal path does not record a fresh checkpoint at the live head the way the legacy path does (MatchRecovery's `cache.record(...)` block). A journal-path recovery therefore loses checkpoint acceleration on the NEXT boot. Not a correctness issue and deliberately out of this slice; worth folding into S5/S6 when the journal path becomes the only path.
